claim: Patchline publishes a public roadmap board where every planned feature links to a real public-repository failure mode, a proof gate, and an expected artifact. The board is regenerated from pinned public-code analyses rather than maintained as an unverifiable wish list.

planned_features.title: Monthly reproducibility reports
planned_features.why: Rerun public gates on a cadence and publish cache status, failures, fixes, and benchmark trends.

planned_features.title: Contributor recognition
planned_features.why: Recognize new real-repo slices, ecosystem parsers, false-positive reductions, and artifact improvements.

planned_features.title: Release-quality capstone demo
planned_features.why: Show a fresh user downloading unfamiliar repos, finding high-signal risks, generating bounded interventions, rejecting bad output, and regenerating evidence.

planned_features.title: Ecosystem parser showcase
planned_features.why: Make parser coverage visible by ecosystem, framework, fixture, fuzz seed, and real-repo proof.

planned_features.title: Runtime evidence bridge
planned_features.why: Link traces, logs, deploy markers, and incident exports back to repository-native data-change findings.

planned_features.title: Reviewer evidence bundles
planned_features.why: Package claims, limitations, figures, case studies, and generated intervention outcomes into paper-review-ready bundles.
